design: Under attack: "Execution-only self-learning loop over a pre-decided daily trade list" — episode = one parent-fixed order (asset/side/size) with a hard deadline T∈{15,30,60} min; state = (time-left, inventory-left) + (spread, top imbalance, 5-min |ret|/vol, hour, frozen-mid flag); actions = post at touch / 1 tick behind / join+cross / cancel-replace, MANDATORY market cross at T; reward = −implementation shortfall vs decision mid incl. fees; learner = Nevmyvaka-style backward induction or a contextual bandit (explicitly NOT MuZero, no tree); training data = real micro-notional ($5–10) post-only orders via the 907 recorder + D65 phase-2 rails; deliverable = a measured maker cost tier replacing fee16/slip5 plus a two-line rule. Claimed ceiling +0.11 Sharpe (21→8 bp on a 0.155/day book), learned increment over the rule 1–4 bp/side, P(changes any goalposts verdict) ≈ 0 by the proposal's own account.
lens: AMPLIFIER-NOT-SOURCE: assume the loop only amplifies the information in its realized-shortfall targets; ask what the learned object carries that a direct estimator (fee-schedule lookup, per-state fill-rate table, ridge on 806 minute features, closed-form controller) does not; re-do the arithmetic; check gross/net, in-sample/OOS, size regime and fee tier in every literature number; default refuted when uncertain.
strongest_objection: The proposal's own decomposition already concedes the lens: "a direct estimator ... gives the SAME quantity once the state grid is fixed" and the ceiling is +0.11 Sharpe against a +0.97 bar. Pushed one step further, the concession becomes a refutation of the design AS A LOOP. Under a martingale mid, the paired saving of "post at touch, cross at T" over "taker now" is, by optional stopping (E[mid at min(τ,T)] = mid_0), exactly p·(s + Δf): p = P(through-fill by T), s = full spread, Δf = taker − maker fee. Every term is a schedule constant (Δf: 12–15 bp/side at Kraken tiers 5–10 on the July-2026 ladder, fetched 2026-09-05), a directly observed quantity (s), or a per-state frequency (p) — nothing to learn. The Nevmyvaka DP earns its 27.16–35.50% (full read of rlexec.pdf: V = 5k/10k shares, H = 2/8 min, S&L cost = impact, "we assume that commissions and exchange fees are negligible") by SPLITTING a large order to reduce impact; at venue-minimum size the order cannot be split (I ∈ {0,1}, not the "8 inventory levels" in the compute paragraph), impact is nil by construction, and waiting weakly dominates crossing early, so the DP collapses to the two-line rule. The only remaining "information" is the departure from martingale — E[mid_T − mid_0 | state] ≠ 0 — which is a minute-horizon conditional MEAN, i.e. the 806/811 linear_xs signal (OOS IC +0.13/+0.15/+0.17 at H=1 by vol tercile, +0.14 at H=5, +0.060 at H=20, `runs/806_predictability_probe/result.md:44-46,74,103`; nonlinear ≤ linear per 811). Its execution value is bounded by IC × σ_h ≈ 0.15 × 7–13 bp ≈ 1–2 bp at H=1 and ≈ 0.06 × 43 bp ≈ 2.6 bp at H=20 — the proposal's own "1–4 bp/side", obtainable by a ridge on already-measured features. So the "self-learning loop" is a fee lookup + a fill-rate table + a ridge forecast the record already owns. It also does not answer the operator's question (a loop that learns patterns to serve Monte Carlo search): the proposal removes the Monte Carlo and the loop and keeps only a cost measurement. Second, the deployable artifact (a) — "a measured cost tier that replaces fee16/slip5" — cannot be produced by the instrument: the book is equal-weight over ~240–268 live assets in 2024–26 (`POWERED_RESULT.md:33-34`), so the four recorded majors carry ≈ 4/268 ≈ 1.5% of its turnover; the tier measured on BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP says nothing about where 98.5% of the cost is paid. Third, the design's load-bearing escape from the HOLD attractor — a mandatory MARKET cross at T after a 15–60-minute rest — is forbidden by the very rails it says it reuses ("never a market order, ever"; auto-cancel after 1–2 bars: `tasks/TASK_907_LIVE_FILL_PROBE.md:629-632`, `phase2_rails.py:41,170-177`), so step 1 needs a new safety regime and operator ruling, not a reuse.
amplifier_check: VERDICT: pure amplifier; creates no information. (1) Target = realized shortfall per order. Conditional on state, its expectation is p(state)·(s + Δf) plus the minute-horizon drift term. Δf is a lookup (Kraken Pro ladder fetched 2026-09-05, tiers effective 2026-07-09: $50k 0.15/0.30, $100k 0.12/0.25, $250k 0.10/0.22, $500k 0.08/0.20, $1M 0.06/0.18, $2.5M 0.04/0.15 — gap 11–15 bp; tiers 1–2 0.40/0.80 and 0.30/0.60 — gap 30–40 bp). s is observed on every book event (`recorder.py:103` book+trade, depth 10). p(state) is a frequency table; 907 step 0 already gives its optimistic bound (through-print proxy, `PREREGISTRATION.md:44-64`). (2) The DP adds nothing at micro size: with a single indivisible order and no impact, the Bellman recursion has one non-trivial decision ("cross now vs wait") and under a martingale the value of waiting is ≥ 0 each minute (adds fill mass × (s+Δf)); the literature's DP gains (Nevmyvaka +27–35%, Hendricks–Wilcox ≤10.3%, Ning et al. 0–12 bp of TWAP P&L, all institutional size with assumed or simulated impact) are impact-splitting gains and do not transfer. (3) The state-conditional residue is the 806 conditional mean — a FORECAST — already measured linear-optimal; a ridge is the direct estimator, and "on-policy collection" adds nothing because the fill outcome of a micro order does not change the mid path (the proposal's own Nevmyvaka independence claim). (4) Worth at daily IC ≈ 0: identical to the proposal's own number and independent of the loop — the saving is a cost constant. Arithmetic re-checked: 0.1551 × 365 = 56.6 → 21 bp/side = 1189 bp = 11.9%/yr; gross +0.74 → net@21 +0.56 implies σ_book ≈ 66%/yr; 21→12 bp = +0.077, 21→8 bp = +0.11, whole stack +0.18 (`POWERED_RESULT.md:49`, `trader/backtest.py:189`). None of it can cross zero on a gross-≤0 book, move the PIT CI [−0.13,+1.23] off zero, or make BEAR-positive. The 4-majors coverage (1.5% of turnover) means even the cost constant is measured for the wrong assets.

surviving_claim: What stands is a static-rule COST MEASUREMENT, not a learning loop, and it is second to a bookkeeping fix: (1) FIRST, record the operator's actual Kraken tier (30-day volume or assets-on-platform) — on the July-2026 ladder the base tier is 0.40/0.80 and the record's 21 bp corresponds to ≥$1M/30d or $1M AoP; if the account sits lower, every net@21 column in the record is optimistic and THAT is the finding. (2) Given the tier, the maker–taker gap is a schedule fact of 11–15 bp/side at tiers 5–10 (30–40 bp at tiers 1–2); a "post-only at the touch, cross at T" rule on a 0.155/day book is worth ≈ p·(s+Δf)·56.6 bp/yr ≈ +0.07..+0.12 Sharpe at p ≈ 0.8–1.0 on liquid pairs — bounded, forecast-free, incapable of moving any goalpost, and estimable from 907's through-print proxy at zero money (step 0). (3) The only measurable unknowns are p (true through-fill rate at the touch within T) and the adverse-selection markout for the ~250-asset TAIL where the book's turnover lives; 907's four majors cover ≈1.5% of that turnover, so any real-order phase must be re-scoped to a sample of tail pairs and labelled by regime, and it requires a new rail ruling (market cross at T, multi-bar rests) rather than the D65 rails. (4) Any state-conditional increment over the rule is the 806 minute forecast repurposed as execution timing — 1–4 bp/side, obtainable by ridge on existing features, no loop; it is a legitimate "execution alpha" arm inside the tactics panel's row 2, not a self-learning design. (5) None of this should be scheduled before TASK_915's G-A read (D79); on G-A FAIL its value is a −0.18 → −0.07 improvement on a book with no edge.
kill_experiment_critique: Sound parts: paired arms so the price path cancels; pre-registration; Newey–West SE; "step 0 can only kill"; tier lookup as a prerequisite. Defects: (K1) is a fee-schedule test, not a learning test — under a martingale the saving is p·(s+Δf), and with Δf = 11–15 bp it clears 5 bp whenever p ≥ 0.4; step 0 on the existing capture already yields p's optimistic bound, so 30–60 days of real orders and an engineer-week confirm a lookup. (K2) is underpowered by construction: with the stated paired std 15–25 bp and n ≈ 1,200, a quintile holds ~240 orders → SE ≈ 20/√240 ≈ 1.3 bp, best-minus-worst SE ≈ 1.8 bp, so a TRUE 3 bp spread reads t ≈ 1.6 and fails the t ≥ 3 bar; t ≥ 3 on 3 bp needs ≈ 4,000 orders (~50 days at the proposed 80/day) BEFORE Bonferroni over a 6-variable × 5-quintile grid; the pre-registered read "no state-conditional surface" would therefore be a false negative dressed as a kill. Order flow is synthetic: 4 pairs × 2 sides × 10 slots/day is not the book's flow (~19 sign-flip orders/day spread over ~250 assets, 4/268 on majors); the measured tier cannot be labelled "for the book". Missing arms: the live trader's existing rule (`config/real_trade_config.py:20,23` — limit, then market after 60 s), a mid-price/inside-spread post, and T beyond 60 min (the parent rebalances once a day; nothing forces a 60-min deadline). Missing pre-commitment: what the row concludes if the tier lookup returns tier ≤ 4 (taker 35–80 bp) — the honest consequence is a re-grade of the record's net columns, not an execution saving. Rails: step 1 needs market crosses and 15–60-bar rests, both forbidden by `TASK_907:629-632` / `phase2_rails.py:170-177`; the "existing rails" cost estimate is wrong and a new D-row plus safety panel is the real cost (907 B2 has already consumed four factory runs on denomination defects). Regime: one 30–60-day window in one regime; adverse selection of resting orders is worst in fast moves, and the pass/fail does not condition on regime. Literature calibration: every cited increment of a learner over a rule (Nevmyvaka, Ning, Hendricks–Wilcox, Schnaubelt) is measured under the paper's own impact simulator at institutional size; none is a live A/B, and none applies at micro size — the proposal's "P(learned beats rule by ≥2–3 bp) ≈ 20–30%" has no supporting datum at this size regime; the direct ridge on 806 features is the right comparator and would make the "learner" redundant even if K2 passed.
